I want to share my recent experience with @fundingpips regarding my $25K 2-Step Flex Master Account.

My account was breached for Maximum Daily Loss. The calculated threshold was $960.71, while my recorded loss was $964.44 — only $3.73 above the threshold.

I want to be completely honest about my mistake. That day, I did not check my dashboard to verify the exact Daily Loss threshold. I genuinely believed my $25K account had a $1,000 daily loss allowance, so I continued trading with that understanding.

I accept that I should have checked the dashboard.

However, I also want to explain where my misunderstanding came from.

A $25K account at 4% equals $1,000, so that was the number I understood as my Daily Loss allowance. What I didn't properly understand was that the 4% is applied dynamically to the higher of the opening balance or opening equity for that particular trading day.

In my case:

$24,017.72 × 4% = $960.71

To be clear, I'm not claiming FundingPips manually changed my limit from $1,000 to $960.71. I understand now that the rule is dynamic.

My mistake was not checking the dashboard that day and not realizing that my actual threshold had become $960.71.

But this is where I believe the system can be confusing for traders. If a $25K account initially makes you understand the Daily Loss as $1,000, the actual dollar threshold can later be lower depending on the opening equity.

I contacted support, acknowledged my mistake, and asked whether there could be any reasonable consideration because the breach was only $3.73 above the calculated threshold.

I was told that the breach was valid and that no exception could be made.

I understand that firms need strict risk rules, and I'm not saying the mathematics were wrong. My mistake was not checking the dashboard.

But I also believe this experience highlights how important it is for traders to understand that the dollar Daily Loss amount is not necessarily fixed and can change based on the applicable opening balance/equity each day.

I'm sharing this so other traders don't make the same mistake I did.

Always check your exact Daily Loss threshold before trading — don't assume the original dollar amount is fixed.
